title: The shape of every game
kind: a build chapter: the practice game, with the parts every game shares
one: You build a short practice game with the 3 parts that every game in Summit Ready shares. They are the dark strip along the top, the play area and the Round over box. Then the map opens it from the first summit.

stages.title: See the shape that every game shares

screens.title: Look at the 3 parts of every game window

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know the 3 parts that every game window in Summit Ready has.
The 8 games play in 8 different ways, but every game window has the same shape. A player who learns one game knows where to look in the next one.

screenshot.alt: The practice game window, with the dark strip, the question and 3 answer buttons, and the white Round over box in the middle
screenshot.cap: The practice game, with the Round over box showing after the round.

blocks.p: **The dark strip** runs along the top. It shows the game's name, what to do, the points, the speaker picture and **Back to the map**.
**The [[play area|4]]** fills the rest of the window. This is the only part that is different in each game.
**The [[Round over box|5]]** is hidden until the round ends. Then it shows the score, what went well and what went wrong, and a second **Back to the map** button.
When a round ends, the game packs the score and feedback into a GameResult and hands it to the map. The map ticks the summit, and chapter 10 shows the feedback from every game together.
In this chapter, you build the 3 parts around a one-question practice game. Each game chapter then copies the strip and the box from your practice game.

The line `// each game chapter adds its own case below this line` in `frmMap.cs` (chapter 8).
The Icons folder inside Images, and the Sounds folder, both inside bin\Debug (chapter 2). The Sounds folder holds `win.wav` and `lose.wav`.
About 2 hours. Your ticks are kept, so you can stop at the end of any screen and come back later.

words: A `List<string>` holds any number of pieces of text, in order. It can grow: `.Add` puts one more piece on the end.
A button with `Enabled = false` is greyed out, and clicking it does nothing.
A control with `Visible = false` is hidden while the game runs. The designer still shows it, so you can change it.
Puts a control in front of every other control on the window.
The part of a game window under the dark strip, where the game itself is played.
The white box that shows the score and the feedback when a round ends.
blocks.intro: You do not need to learn these words now. Where you first meet each one in the chapter, it has a dotted line under it. Hover over it or tap it to see what it means.

blocks.p: The Round over box has room for 3 lines in each list. ListText gives up to 3 lines, then one line that counts the rest. It says **1 more thing** or **2 more things**, so the words always fit the number.

code.title: ListText
partLines: An empty list
An empty list gives **Nothing this time.**
Up to 3 lines
The loop, which repeats the same steps for each line, stops at the end of the list or after 3 lines. Each line starts with a dash and ends with a new line.
The rest
`more` is how many lines did not fit. If it is 1, the line says **1 more thing**. If it is 2 or more, it says **2 more things**.

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, both **Back to the map** buttons close the window, and the window asks first if the round is not over.
A player who leaves before the round ends scores nothing for that summit. So FormClosing, the code that runs as the window closes, asks first, unless the result is already kept.

code.title: btnBack_Click, btnDone_Click and frmPractice_FormClosing
partLines: Back on the strip
**Back to the map** on the strip closes the window, which runs FormClosing.
Back in the Round over box
The gold button in the Round over box does the same.
Ask first
A finished round closes at once. Otherwise a Yes and No message asks. No sets `e.Cancel` to true, which keeps the window open.

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you know that every part of the practice game works, including the click it must refuse.
Run each test with F5. Tick each test when it passes. The test marked as a click to refuse must do nothing, and that counts as a pass.

check.what: Open the practice game from the map, then click **Back to the map** on the strip before answering.
check.how: A message asks whether to leave. **No** keeps the game open. **Yes** goes back to the map with no tick.
check.fix: Check the code of frmPractice_FormClosing. Then click frmPractice in the designer, click the lightning bolt in Properties and check that frmPractice_FormClosing is beside **FormClosing**.

check.what: Click one answer, then click a different answer.
check.how: The second click does nothing. The answers are grey after the first click.
check.fix: Check the 3 lines in Answer_Click that set `Enabled = false`.

check.what: Click an answer, then **See my score**.
check.how: The Round over box shows the score, with a line under What went well or What went wrong.
check.fix: Check the code of btnScore_Click and ShowRoundOver. Then click btnScore in the designer, click the lightning bolt in Properties and check that btnScore_Click is beside **Click**.

check.what: Click an answer, then close the window with the X before clicking **See my score**.
check.how: The window closes with no question. The map shows a tick on Slieve Binnian.
check.fix: Check that RecordResult ends with `KeepResult();`, and that KeepResult sets `finished = true;`.

check.what: Click the speaker picture on the practice game's strip.
check.how: The picture changes to the muted speaker. It stays muted on the map.
check.fix: Click picSound on frmPractice in the designer, click the lightning bolt in Properties and check that picSound_Click is beside **Click**.

screens.title: Your turn: ask a question from your own topic

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, the practice game asks a question from your own topic, and you have tested it.
The practice game asks how high Slieve Donard is. Change it to a question from your own topic, with 3 answers to pick from.

code.title: A question from your own topic
code.text: private string rightAnswer = "Salsa";   // the answer that scores
task: Change the Text of lblQuestion to your own question.
Change the Text of btnAnswer1, btnAnswer2 and btnAnswer3 to your 3 answers. Only one of them is right.
Change `rightAnswer` to the right answer, typed exactly as it is on its button.
Change the 2 result lines in Answer_Click, and the 2 feedback lines in RecordResult, so they fit your question.
code.test: Press F5, open the practice game from the map and click your right answer.
code.expect: The result line says the answer is right, and **See my score** shows 100 out of 100 points.
code.hint: Every line that says 850 m or Slieve Donard needs to change. There are 5 of them in the code.

blocks.p: The finished code shows the right answer for a dance game. Your own right answer goes in its place.
Chapter 11 replaces the practice game, if you build that chapter. So keep this question short.

glossary: A `List<string>` holds any number of pieces of text, in order. It can grow: `.Add` puts one more piece on the end.
A button with `Enabled = false` is greyed out, and clicking it does nothing.
A control with `Visible = false` is hidden while the game runs. The designer still shows it, so you can change it.
Puts a control in front of every other control on the window.
The part of a game window under the dark strip, where the game itself is played.
The white box that shows the score and the feedback when a round ends.
